data.source_title: 2142. Understanding Errors in Sterile Processing of Surgical Instruments That Lead to Need for Immediate Use Sterilization in the Operating Room
data.locator: Abstract, Methods and Results; prospective 30-day SPD study of tray errors associated with immediate-use sterilization
data.source_setting: Hospital sterile processing department and operating rooms; institution type/size not stated in report
data.source_evidence_basis: In 30 days the department processed 17,348 trays for 1,868 procedures and identified 86 errors: 38 assembly, 30 sterilization, 10 case-cart, and 8 other. Ten assembly errors involved missing or incorrect instruments.
data.limitations: Short single-site study; error counts are not independently reported denominators by category, and identified errors were those associated with immediate-use sterilization. Do not treat as a general defect rate or RWJ estimate. This source is a published conference abstract, not a full-length study report.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as examples of assembly, sterilization-documentation, and case-cart failure states that can trigger rework or urgent instrument handling. Do not model routine throughput or local error probabilities from these counts.

data.source_title: 2142. Understanding Errors in Sterile Processing of Surgical Instruments That Lead to Need for Immediate Use Sterilization in the Operating Room
data.locator: Background, Methods and Conclusion; tray assembly, sterilization, and cart error categories; local immediate-use process description
data.source_setting: Single hospital SPD and operating rooms
data.quantity: Sterile instrument workflow error classes and response pressure
value: Tray assembly errors (including missing/incorrect instruments and filter placement)
Immediate-use sterilization as a response to an instrument problem
data.source_evidence_basis: Investigators grouped observed events into assembly, sterilization, case-cart, and other errors; they identify process improvement opportunities in tray assembly to reduce immediate-use sterilization events.
data.limitations: The article describes one institution and its locally defined immediate-use cycle; it does not establish standard practice, routine cycle duration, or RWJ workflow. This source is a published conference abstract, not a full-length study report.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent unavailable or incorrect tray contents, sterilization documentation hold, and missing case-cart tray as distinct events that may prompt correction or escalation. Model emergency sterilization only if local policy validates the pathway.
